Is there a reason to do this loopback?  If the modbus device can self-describe all of its interfaces, why do the bounceback through entity-manager?  Just have the modbus daemon host all the inventory objects directly?  I don't suspect this patch is "wrong", I suspect there's a use case here that just isn't documented very well.

This brings the design in sync with other inventory daemons such as fru-device and gpio-hw-inventory where EM holds all the configurations and only the required configurations are probed when a specific device is discovered (rather than exposing all the configuration even if the device is not found as these would be part of board configurations). Please refer to designs for complete flow -
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/77318
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/77422

And we don't need to reimplement the logic to expose the inventory interfaces as they are already being exposed through EM.

I am marking this as resolved here and lets discuss any further comments related to this on design doc itself.
Please keep the naming matching the schema contained within the file.

ModbusDevice and ModbusDeviceDetect are two different schema configurations and modbus_device.json will hold all the schema definitions related to modbus devices, hence the name. I see this pattern for other schema files as well, for example, mctp.json. Marking this as resolved for now, please let me know if there are still any concerns.

what is a detect?

this seems to be a combination of probe address and and attributes discovered.

the application protocol specification talked about nodes
+1, I think the only thing wrong here is the "detect" portion.  Detection is supposed to happen pre-entity-manager instantiation, so this would just be "modbus device"
This schema is for pre-entity-manager instantiation only, please refer to design https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/77318 .
This schema represents the initial configuration for modbus probe to discover the modbus inventory. Please refer to design https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/77318 .

huh?

4.4 data model 

there are 4 overlapping data types 
each data is addressed 0-65536
each element within a data block is numbered 1-n

the above is in bold page 7/50

> huh?
> 
> 4.4 data model 
> 
> there are 4 overlapping data types 
> each data is addressed 0-65536
> each element within a data block is numbered 1-n
>

What is the specific question/concern you are raising here?

This address refers to the address of the modbus device in a daisy chain. For exmaple, RS485 can support upto 32 devices in a single segment and can have upto 247 devices with repeaters. So, this address range refers to those devices.

Modbus supports a number of different transports.  Should this be called

ModBusSerialPort
ModBusEthernetPort

Etc, so that we can differentiate the physical hardware?  As written it's not clear what transport this would use.
Please refer to Connection Type (RTU, TCP) property, its already being handled there.

what is this? 

register addresses? (edit: probably not)

did you mean node address?  or unit address in TCP?
why is this a range and not discreet?

are you trying to describe a probe or detection for a device?  looking for a sensor on any of N consecutive addresses?  (why would they be consecutive?  would we not expect to correlate the assigned address with some physical instance uniquely)?
These are register addresses. Refer to Section 4.4 Modbus Addressing Model.

this is missing the node number (serial protocol)

1-247 for serial, 0xFF recommended for tcp

edit: or that is the address range being referred to.

I searched the spec and i couldn't find the word node at all https://www.modbus.org/docs/Modbus_Application_Protocol_V1_1b3.pdf.

The registers and coils have addresses.
see discussion in required properties below
Replying at same place and marking this as resolved.

4.2 address and data are Big endian byte order (most significant byte first) (elsewhere bits are numbered little endian and sent Le in the wire)

do you have non standard devices?
Yes, we have seen devices with both the mixes, hence this property.

why are any of these inventory data items expected to be in registers?

because of the exemplar device?

The modbus spec defines a gateway to read product information objects with this information.
Because as per size requirements only registers can hold them. Refer to Data Model 4.3

formats should determine the endianness and size implicitly.

this doesn't differentiate between input registers and holding registers, and doesn't allow description of digital inputs or coils (digital outputs), the other numbering spaces.

(this means that we won't need to parse/case 3 levels deep when comparing values)
I have moved this inside the registers, so its specific to registers.

Why are we doing the struct-of-arrays thing vs array-of-structs? IMO this strategy makes it less ergonomic and the benefit isn't obvious. But maybe I'm missing something regarding EM's implementation constraints (which maybe we could fix?)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AoS_and_SoA

+1.  Entity-manager uses arrays of structs.  Yes.... the way James (throws under bus) chose to represent these arrays originally isn't the easiest to parse, but it's what we have.  I understand that PDI can't parse these, but that's not a reason to make things a mess here.  Path forward is either:
A. Use the existing code for parsing arrays of structs.
B. Update EM/dbus-sensors to improve how we represent arrays of structs such that it's compatible with PDI
C. Improve PDI to make it handle the (admittedly insane) way that EM hosts arrays on dbus.
Done
For B, maybe https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/79837 can help. Looking forward to any comments 😊

the change log says the interface is intended to be durable to TCP and indeed includes the type but baud rate and parity bits are required but IP address and TCP port are missing.   (I'd expect a URL could be convenient but don't know/didn't look if a scheme has been registered with IANA.  edit: mbap=tcp (udp) port 502, mbap-s= (tls on tcp) port 802, but no mbap was found in url scheme registry).

This is an inventory interface right?

This is an inventory interface. My current use case is only for serial, so i have updated the schema definition to reflect only it, i.e. ModbusRTUDetect. In future when use case for TCP will be there, we will add those.

conversely the interface doesn't specify the electrical interface: is it RS232, RS4285 or something else (which is required to properly connect and determine the possible topology).  

232 and 485 are explicitly mentioned in the modbus API protocol specification (1.1b3  4.1 5/50)


The exemplar device includes a status, readonly register bit that records if the terminator resistor is enabled.  for rs485 its recommended that devices are wired along a linear chain terminated at each end and not a star topology (per wikipedia).
Added Interface in latest patch.

do we want a decorator to the associated serial port?

The exemplar device includes a status, readonly register bit that records if the terminator resistor is enabled.  for rs485 its recommended that devices are wired along a linear chain terminated at each end and not a star topology (per wikipedia).

thinking again, the data parity and baud rate are defined by the network port.

it needs to be common to all modbus servers on the given tty link (or tcp ip address and port).

the network interface (possibly muxing a serial UART to this modbus network) should be a higher common entity to the sensor device (a server exposing multiple readings).

while we could funnel all this configuration through EM, it doesn't appear there is enough standard function in the exemplar sensor to warrant shuffling all the programming interface through entity manager.  

I am advocating separating the device register interface (which registers have which formats, especially for random configuration (unit selection), status (not defined protocol error status) from the instance information describing sensor name, association, and thresholds.
They are already separate as this schema definitions is just for inventory and not for sensors.

It would be great to have an configuration example here.

Or link to a gerrit change which adds a configuration using the schema.
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/81726
Would these make more sense as strings that that enforced hex numbers?  I guess it would require a conversion though.
Yes, it would require conversion. Is there a strict requirement for addresses to be hex strings in EM?
No, not at all, probably just easier to read and review.
